lines.text: Christopher Pinchbeck was a London clockmaker who died in 1732.
lines.say: Christopher PINCH-bek was a London clockmaker who died in seventeen thirty two.

lines.text: His Fleet Street shop sold clocks and musical automata.
He is credited with a copper and zinc alloy that imitated gold.
It was mostly copper with some zinc, and far cheaper than gold.
Makers used it for watch cases and snuff boxes.
It stayed bright for a good while but darkens with age.
After 1732 his son Edward carried on selling the metal.

post.caption: Pinchbeck: a clockmaker's imitation gold. Christopher Pinchbeck was a London clockmaker who died in 1732. His Fleet Street shop sold clocks and musical automata. He is credited with a copper and zinc alloy that imitated gold. It was mostly copper with some zinc, and far cheaper than gold. Makers used it for watch cases and snuff boxes. It stayed bright for a good while but darkens with age. After 1732 his son Edward carried on selling the metal. The word pinchbeck is first recorded in the 1730s. It did not come to mean sham until the 1790s.
